# DiceTable

> DiceTable is a free browser tool for comparing tabletop dice rolls by their exact probability. Build a table of named rolls, read the full distribution and summary stats for each, and overlay them on one chart to compare and balance them.

DiceTable is for tabletop and strategy gamers who want to understand and balance dice rolls without learning a scripting language or any statistics. It works with any system, because a roll is just a dice expression. Everything happens in a graphical table: there is no notation to memorize first and no math background required.

## What it computes

All probabilities are exact. DiceTable enumerates each die's distribution and combines them by full convolution, so every number is the true probability of that outcome. It does not use normal or uniform approximations, and it does not sample or simulate to produce its stats.

A roll can be scored two ways. Sum mode adds the dice into one total. Pool mode counts successes instead: each die succeeds when it meets a threshold (for example, 8 or higher on a d10), the result is the number of successes, and the flat modifier grants or removes successes directly (a result never drops below zero). Pool odds are exact too, including rerolls.

For each roll it reports:

- Mean (the long-run average result).
- Standard deviation and variance (how spread out or consistent the results are).
- Mode (the most likely result, or results when several tie).
- Range (the smallest and largest possible results).
- Hit probability (how often the roll meets a target you set).

## Dice notation it understands

DiceTable reads standard tabletop dice notation, edited inline in the table:

- Count and die, such as 3d8 (roll three eight-sided dice and add them).
- Flat modifier, such as +2 or -1, added to the total.
- Keep highest or lowest, such as 4d6kh3 (roll four six-sided dice, keep the highest 3) or klN.
- Reroll specific faces, once or always, such as r1 or r<3.
- Explode a chosen face, such as !6 (on that face, roll again and add), with a depth cap that keeps results readable.
- Count successes (dice pools), shown as count ≥8 or count ≤2: the roll's result is how many dice meet the threshold, and the flat modifier becomes auto-successes (+2 auto). Keep and explode apply only to summed rolls.

## Roll modes

A roll mode applies to the whole expression:

- Normal (roll once).
- Advantage (roll twice and take the higher result).
- Disadvantage (roll twice and take the lower result).

Roll modes affect summed rolls only. A pool roll keeps its setting for when it switches back to summing, but counting successes ignores it.

## Comparing and balancing rolls

Every row appears in an overlay chart with its own color. The chart has four views:

- PMF: how likely each exact result is.
- CDF: the chance of rolling at most a given number.
- CCDF: the chance of rolling at least a given number, useful for "beat the DC" checks.
- Target: per-row hit-rate bars once you set one or more target numbers.

Summed rolls and pool rolls chart on separate panels, because their axes mean different things: one shows totals, the other counts successes.

You can set up to five targets (for example armor classes or save DCs) and choose how a roll is compared to them: at least, greater than, at most, less than, or exactly. A Hit % column then shows how often each summed roll meets each target. Pool rolls answer to a separate shared pool target ("at least n successes") instead. A built-in roller can also simulate any summed roll, using the same exact odds the chart shows.

A dedicated Target hit view compares every roll against all of your targets at once, three ways. A grid shows each roll's hit chance per target, color-coded from reliable to long shot and sortable by any target column. Curves plot each summed roll's hit chance for every possible target value, with your current targets marked. Bars show one panel per target with rolls ranked by hit chance. Pool rolls appear in the grid and bars under the shared pool target.

## Privacy

DiceTable runs entirely in your browser. Your rolls and settings are stored on your own device, and the site collects only anonymous analytics. There are no accounts.

## Links

- [DiceTable](https://dice-table.app/): the app itself.
- [Docs](https://dice-table.app/docs): a quickstart walkthrough, a glossary of every term, and a page explaining the math (convolution, PMF, CDF, CCDF, and the stat formulas).
- [Privacy](https://dice-table.app/privacy): what the site does and does not collect.
